subject: general
question: A dealer allowed a 50% discount on an article and still managed a 71% profit. Find the ratio of the cost price to the listed price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discount 50% → SP = 50% of LP

Profit 71% → SP = 171% of CP

So 0.5 LP = 1.71 CP

CP/LP = 0.5 / 1.71 = 50 / 171

**∴ Answer = 50 : 171**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount = 50%, Profit = 71%

**Formula used:**

SP = LP × (1 − Discount), SP = CP × (1 + Profit)

**Calculation:**

⇒ SP = 0.5 × LP

⇒ SP = 1.71 × CP

⇒ 0.5 LP = 1.71 CP

⇒ CP / LP = 0.5 / 1.71

⇒ = 50 / 171

**∴ The required ratio is 50 : 171.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Discount Formula

SP = LP × (1 − discount/100)

Profit Formula

SP = CP × (1 + profit/100)

Ratio Formation

Equate both SP expressions to relate CP and LP.

Shortcut Insight

Convert percentages to multipliers for quick solving.
